confidence_rationale: Optoelectronic plethysmography and oesophageal/gastric pressures in 11 adults during film-induced laughter: every fit was a sudden run of repetitive expiratory efforts at 4.6 +/- 1.1 Hz, lasting 3.7 +/- 2.2 s, and drove lung volume ~1.5 L below FRC with dynamic airway compression. This confirms the respiratory premise in MECH-110's notes (laughter is a high-frequency expiratory override far above resting rate). It also cuts against the per-exhalation mechanism: ~4-5 pulses per second is a stereotyped mechanical run, faster than the ~600 ms cognitive resolution component, and more naturally explained by a brainstem pattern generator than by one threat/resolution cycle per pulse. Hence mixed.
failure_signatures: Expiratory pulses run at ~4.6 Hz (about 220 ms each), shorter than the ERP resolution component (~600 ms), which makes it implausible that each pulse carries a separate cognitive threat-activation/resolution cycle.
Fits are stereotyped mechanical events (sudden onset, monotonic volume drop below FRC), consistent with a released motor programme rather than a sequence of individually gated decisions.
No cognitive, affective or threat measure was taken, so the respiratory pattern cannot be linked to any resolution sequence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Fits of laughter are characterised by a sudden run of repetitive expiratory efforts at ~4.6 Hz lasting ~3.7 s, producing a ~1.55 L drop below functional residual capacity and marked dynamic airway compression, with the diaphragm actively limiting pressure transmission.
mapping.ree_translation: Confirms that laughter is a high-frequency expiratory override of the resting respiratory rhythm, the respiratory substrate that MECH-110 (via MECH-107/MECH-108) treats as a rapid series of forced plan-sweep clearings.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures respiratory mechanics only. Treating each ~220 ms expiratory pulse as a plan-sweep tag-clear is REE's interpretation; the pulse rate and stereotypy fit a motor pattern generator better than per-pulse cognitive cycling. Small N, a single comedic stimulus, lab setting.
mapping.source_context: 11 healthy adults watching comedy film clips (Roberto Benigni); optoelectronic plethysmography of chest-wall compartments and, in 7 subjects, oesophageal and gastric pressures.

confidence_components.notes: Rigorous physiology, small N. Supports the respiratory premise, weakens the per-pulse-cycle mechanism by timescale argument (cross-referenced with Chan 2013 / Shibata 2017 resolution timing).
